alex.t: heads-up — PR #4822 proposes switching to a single structured rate header to reduce header churn. quick check: would this break any SDKs or infra that parse specific headers (X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset)?

jamal: can you paste the proposed header format?

alex.t: sure — plan is to add an optional header `X-Redwood-Quota` with comma-separated k=v pairs per-route, e.g.
```
X-Redwood-Quota: route=chat,limit=1000,window=60,burst=200,remaining=77
```
and the response body on 429 would include a small JSON quota hint for modern clients: `{"retry_after":12, "quota":{"route":"chat","remaining":77}}`

sara: I like the compactness. main concern: older clients currently read `X-RateLimit-Remaining` directly. if we remove those it'll break them. are we planning dual headers?

alex.t: good point. PR currently *adds* `X-Redwood-Quota` and keeps the old headers for now, but there was a suggestion to deprecate old ones later.

jamal: from runtime side, adding both is cheap. but two notes: 1) if `burst` semantics are per-route, we need to ensure we emit the right burst value for dedicated vs hosted (they differ). 2) SDK parsing needs to tolerate either header order and parsing failure.

mike.ops: small ops note — some edge CDNs strip unusually long headers or reorder. the comma-separated form should be fine but avoid embedding spaces after commas.

alex.t: noted — we'll avoid spaces. also planning a migration window: dual-write for 90 days + feature flag to stop old header.

sara: SDK action items: update clients to prefer `X-Redwood-Quota` parsing, fall back to existing `X-RateLimit-*`. also handle missing numeric fields gracefully (treat missing remaining as unknown). i'll open a PR on the node/python sdks after the runtime change lands.

jamal: test plan from runtime: add unit tests that verify both headers present, and an integration test that sends traffic to dedicated pool to ensure burst is correct. i'll add a smoke test that asserts the JSON body `quota.route` matches request route.

alex.t: CI heads-up — @ci-bot flagged one failing test in your branch, jamal: "rateheader-format-test" fails when header ordering changes.

ci-bot: build 4822/7 — rateheader-format-test failed (timeout). logs: `AssertionError: expected X-RateLimit-Remaining, got X-Redwood-Quota` — looks like a test trying to parse a single legacy header.

jamal: thanks — i'll relax the test to accept either header and re-run.

mike.ops: one more thing: docs + changelog need to include the exact grammar for `X-Redwood-Quota` so third-party proxies can parse it. also we need to call out that the header is advisory and not authoritative for enforcement (enforcement is server-side).

sara: agree. i'll update SDK README and add a short migration note: "Prefer X-Redwood-Quota; if absent, fall back to legacy X-RateLimit-*; treat missing numbers as unknown and implement exponential backoff on 429s."

alex.t: sweet. final ask: can eng-runtime and sdks merge their PRs within the same release window? if yes i'll mark the runtime PR for canary tomorrow.

jamal: aiming for canary tomorrow morning. i'll ping here when the canary deploy is up.

sara: i'll hold off the SDK release until you confirm canary.

alex.t: thanks all — follow-ups: jamal to relax tests + deploy canary, sara to draft SDK PR + docs, mike.ops to add CDN note in docs. i'll add the migration timeline to the PR description. :thumbsup:
